items.title: JSON Schema 2020-12 and the Contract for Context | ​Ola Hungerford | MCP Release Party - Seattle
items.summary:
Session 2: Say What You Mean: JSON Schema 2020-12 and the Contract for Context

​In MCP, the schema is the contract for context. It's how a tool tells a model what goes in and what comes out. MCP originally shipped a three-keyword subset of JSON Schema, a reasonable bet on the lowest common denominator across a fragmented landscape of LLM APIs. Two SEPs later, tool schemas conform to JSON Schema 2020-12, the same default dialect as OpenAPI 3.1. This talk will cover examples of what that unlocks, what it doesn't fix, and what client and server authors need to change in the new specification.

​About Speaker:
​Ola Hungerford is a Principal Engineer at Nordstrom and a maintainer and community moderator for the Model Context Protocol. She leads AI enablement initiatives while contributing to MCP's specification, developer tooling, documentation, and community governance. Ola comes from a diverse technical background spanning two decades, including personalisation systems and enterprise platforms. She's also a vocalist and songwriter who experiments with augmenting human creativity through technology.

About the Event:
This session was presented at the MCP Release Party hosted on July 28th at Microsoft Reactor in Seattle area. ​This event was hosted as a part of a series of MCP Release Parties taking place simultaneously in cities around the world.

items.title: MCP Goes Stateless | ​John Dellenbaugh & Pankaj Kumar | MCP Release Party - Seattle
items.summary:
​Session 1: MCP Goes Stateless

​The new MCP specification (2026-07-28) makes the protocol stateless. We will break down what this change is, why it matters, and then dig into it together with a live demo.

​About Speakers:
​John Dellenbaugh is a Software Engineering Manager, most recently at Microsoft, where he spent 19 years delivering cloud, security, and AI work with a hands-on background in software security, network security, and Zero Trust identity. He now works as a founding engineer at an early-stage AI startup on MCP architecture, vector search, and agent workflows.

​Pankaj Kumar is a Software Developer at Amazon with a deep interest in MLOps, especially the infrastructure and emerging standards for running AI agents in production. Outside of work, he is a big fan of Lord of the Rings, anime, and manga.

About the Event:
This session was presented at the MCP Release Party hosted on July 28th at Microsoft Reactor in Seattle area. ​This event was hosted as a part of a series of MCP Release Parties taking place simultaneously in cities around the world.

items.title: Events Notifications in MCP | ​Aman Singh | MCP Release Party - Seattle
items.summary:
​Session 4: Events Notifications in MCP

​MCP, the protocol agents use to reach tools and data, can notify a client only while it holds a connection open, and mostly only that something changed, not what. That's about to change. An MCP working group is drafting Events, an upcoming protocol extension that lets agents subscribe to structured event streams. This talk is a brief tour of the proposal and how it is going to shape real-time events in MCP.

​About Speaker:
​Aman Singh is a Principal Software Engineer in the Office of Azure's CTO, where he focuses on Agentic Software Engineering and is a maintainer of Drasi, a CNCF Sandbox project for change-driven architectures. He has had more than 12 years of distributed systems experience at LinkedIn and Microsoft, spanning stream processing (Kafka, Samza), cloud migration, and building new Azure services from the ground up.

About the Event:
This session was presented at the MCP Release Party hosted on July 28th at Microsoft Reactor in Seattle area. ​This event was hosted as a part of a series of MCP Release Parties taking place simultaneously in cities around the world.

items.title: Policy Enforcement and Tamper-Evident Audit Chains | ​Imran Siddique | MCP Release Party - Seattle
items.summary:
Session 3: Governed MCP: Policy Enforcement and Tamper-Evident Audit Chains

​MCP servers today have no built-in way to enforce policy or prove what happened after the fact. This session walks through cMCP, an open-source gateway that wraps any MCP server without requiring changes to it, enforcing Cedar policies before each tool call and chaining every call into a tamper-evident record. We'll cover how it works, see it running against a live server, and discuss where this fits into the broader MCP ecosystem as adoption grows.

​About Speaker:
​Imran Siddique is Chief Platform Officer at Opaque Systems and creator of the Agent Governance Toolkit, an open-source project (github.com/microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit) with ~5k GitHub stars positioned for the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation. He founded agentrust-io (github.com/agentrust-io), an open standards initiative behind Agent Manifest and Confidential MCP. Imran spent 18 years across various parts of Microsoft Azure, most recently leading agentic AI architecture and engineering strategy on Azure Core Engineering. He's a published author who treats governance as an engineering discipline, not a checkbox.

About the Event:
This session was presented at the MCP Release Party hosted on July 28th at Microsoft Reactor in Seattle area. ​This event was hosted as a part of a series of MCP Release Parties taking place simultaneously in cities around the world.

items.title: AI Agents Self-Create Unsafe SKILL.md (CyberSec)
items.summary:
Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, and OpenClaw were paired with skill-evolution systems including EvoSkill, SkillClaw, AutoSkill, SkillsVote, and SkillOpt. The results were devastating. 

What happens when these agents extract the wrong lesson from a successful task? And they do: see my video. 

Discover how one unsafe experience can become a persistent SKILL.md file in your skill library. And influence a completely new AI session after everything else has been reset. 

A newly emerging cybersecurity topic. 

all right w/ authors: 
Practice Makes Unsafe: Skill Misevolution in Self-Improving LLM Agents
Xutao Mao1 Liangjie Zhao2 Xiang Zheng1 Cong Wang1
from
1 City University of Hong Kong
2 Adelaide University

items.title: Are AI Models Escaping On Purpose?
items.summary:
Apparently the newest benchmark for AI models is… can it commit cyber crimes? 😭

First OpenAI’s model broke out during testing and hacked Hugging Face.

Then Anthropic basically showed up like, “our models commit crimes too.”

And now Meta has joined the club after one of its AI models accidentally got access to the public internet during cybersecurity testing and started hacking another company.

Obviously, there are some very real and slightly terrifying implications here about what happens when increasingly capable AI systems get access to tools they weren’t supposed to have.

But I also can’t get over how these stories are starting to feel like a very weird flex from the AI companies like: "Our model is so smart it broke containment too!”

Follow to stay up-to-date with what's happening in the tech and AI world!

#ainews #ai #meta #openai #anthropic

items.title: Two Limits No Model Has Escaped
items.summary: In episode 1017 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, @JonKrohnLearns  talks with Pete Johnson, Field CTO at MongoDB, about why vector search represents the new frontier for AI applications. Pete details how vector search is crucial for RAG pipelines and agentic memory, enabling LLMs to overcome limitations like public data training and knowledge cutoffs, thereby allowing businesses to inject proprietary information and build sophisticated AI agents.

items.title: Set Up Your Account in 5 Steps | H2O.ai Managed Cloud
items.summary:
Follow the full activation path for H2O.ai Managed Cloud, from the invitation email through multi-factor authentication to your first login.

Access to H2O.ai Managed Cloud runs through an External Okta account. This is the identity platform customers and partners use to reach H2O.ai environments and the support portal.

Before you start, your H2O.ai contact is the entry point. If you are evaluating the platform, request access at h2o.ai/demo or through a sales representative, and qualified opportunities may receive a time-bound sandbox. If you are already a customer, your account representative or customer success manager provides access.

Covered in this video:
Step 1: receive your invitation email and find the secure activation link
Step 2: activate your account
Step 3: set a password that meets the criteria
Step 4: configure multi-factor authentication with a security question and an authenticator app
Step 5: reach your environment from the access portal or a custom link

Activation links expire after a limited time. If yours has lapsed, contact your administrator or support@h2o.ai for a new one.

LINKS
H2O.ai University: https://h2o.ai/university
Documentation: https://docs.h2o.ai
Request access or a demo: https://h2o.ai/demo
Support: support@h2o.ai
